analysis: What changed versus the 7:00 AM brief: the selloff accelerated hard in the second hour of the session instead of stabilizing. At about 9:55 AM ET the S&P was -1.40% and the Nasdaq-100 -3.22%; by about 10:57 AM ET the S&P was -3.37% (SPY $740.87), the Nasdaq-100 -5.65% (QQQ $652.77) and the Dow -2.27% (DIA $520.94), wiping out the Dow's early +330-point open gain. The rotation story broke: Apple, the lone megacap green at 7:00 AM (+0.86%), has flipped to -1.13%, and Microsoft (-3.67%), Meta (-6.47%) and Amazon (-4.82%) have joined the slide, so the weakness is no longer contained to chips. The chip complex kept falling into its own hole — AMD -15.95%, Micron -16.58%, Qualcomm -13.95%, the PHLX Semiconductor Index -7.25% and the 3x-long SOXL -34% — and Nvidia (-8.90% to $182.32) picked up a fresh overhang from Reuters reporting about 600,000 H200 chips stuck in Hong Kong awaiting Beijing approval. The political layer thickened: the WSB daily-discussion analysis flags Texas Governor-elect Hinojosa calling for an immediate data-center moratorium, with a UBS estimate that it could affect about 30% of projected 2028 capacity additions — single-source via that analysis, unconfirmed by a second outlet, but it is the kind of headline the tape is trading on. Meanwhile the macro that should help is being ignored: jobless claims fell to 189,000, the fewest since mid-July, and Q3 productivity surged 3.6% with unit labor costs down 0.7%. Gold is bid (+1.5%, ~$4,135) while Bitcoin broke down -5.6% to ~$75,820, and the VIX ETN VXX is +12.34%. Signal vs noise: the broadening of the selloff beyond semis into the megacaps, the memory-complex capitulation and the data-center policy overhang are signal; single-name earnings pops (AppLovin still +28.9%) and WSB's 'AI bubble bursting' rhetoric are noise for the index tape. The next hard catalysts are Friday's payrolls and tonight's after-close earnings (Airbnb, Cloudflare, IREN, Microchip, Monster).

community_signals.takeaway: WSB daily-discussion analysis (09:38-09:56 ET, 1,500 comments) puts sentiment at extreme fear (10-15/100) with semi bulls near capitulation, and surfaces a policy item beyond the headlines: Texas Governor-elect Hinojosa calling for an immediate data-center moratorium, with a UBS estimate that it could affect ~30% of projected 2028 capacity additions. The analysis itself cautions the rhetoric is exaggerated at index level — SPY is far from circuit-breaker territory — and reads the tape as deleveraging of crowded AI positions rather than a market-wide crash.

headlines.headline: The selloff deepened sharply in the second hour of trading: the S&P 500 is -3.37% (SPY $740.87), the Nasdaq-100 -5.65% (QQQ $652.77) and the Dow -2.27% (DIA $520.94) as of about 10:57 AM ET, 15-minute delayed — versus -1.40%, -3.22% and -0.44% at about 9:55 AM ET. The Dow gave back its early 330-point opening gain.
headlines.why_it_matters: The give-back accelerated instead of stabilizing — Wednesday's rally is now more than half unwound at the index level, and the move is broadening.

headlines.headline: AMD fell 15.95% to about $410.91 and Micron fell 16.58% to $663.36 in late-morning trading, deepening from -12.15% and -10.15% at the 7:00 AM brief. The PHLX Semiconductor Index is down 7.25% and the 3x-long semiconductor ETF SOXL is down about 34%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The chip rout is accelerating into its third session, not bottoming — a beat (AMD) and a halted plant (Micron) are both being sold, which says the complex is being repriced, not traded on news.

headlines.headline: Qualcomm fell 13.95% to $149.03 in late-morning trading after its fiscal Q4 handset revenue fell 26% and chip-design margins were guided down to 20-22% from 24% on rising memory costs, despite an EPS beat ($2.17 vs $2.02 expected). At least eight brokerages cut price targets.
headlines.why_it_matters: The memory-cost margin squeeze keeps spreading from memory makers into chip designers — Qualcomm's guide cut plus a wave of target cuts keeps semis leading the market down.

headlines.headline: Nvidia fell 8.90% to $182.32 in late-morning trading (prior close $200.13). Reuters reported today that about 600,000 Nvidia H200 chips are stored in Hong Kong because Beijing has not approved large-scale imports, while CNBC reported Chinese lab Moonshot AI has sought to rent Nvidia's newer Blackwell chips in Europe. Nvidia reports fiscal Q3 on Tuesday, Nov 17, having guided revenue to about $108 billion.
headlines.why_it_matters: A fresh China-demand overhang lands on top of the AI-capex repricing five sessions before Nvidia's report — the tape is de-risking the AI leader, not waiting for the print.

headlines.headline: Tesla fell 11.46% to $341.05 in late-morning trading (prior close $385.19), extending Wednesday's 3.34% slide. Stocktwits retail sentiment on TSLA slipped to 'extremely bearish' with message volume up 107% in 24 hours; analysts flagged political and premium risks to a potential SpaceX merger while Cathie Wood's ARK bought $47 million of SpaceX stock.
headlines.why_it_matters: The political unwind is accelerating — Tesla is now down about 14% across the two sessions since the election result, and the merger-premium story is losing its cushion.

headlines.headline: The megacap split is gone: Apple flipped to -1.13% at $345.57, Microsoft fell 3.67% to $535.40, Meta fell 6.47% to $589.23, Amazon fell 4.82% to $253.21 and Alphabet was -0.51% at about $287.45 (9:52 AM ET). Apple was the lone megacap green at the 7:00 AM brief.
headlines.why_it_matters: The last holdout fell — the selloff is no longer a chip story, it is a broad megacap de-risking, which is what drags the index rather than a sector.

headlines.headline: Memory and storage are the epicenter: SanDisk fell about 13.8%, Western Digital about 12.8% and Seagate about 12.7%, with SK Hynix down 9.4% after falling 9% overnight in Seoul and the Kospi tumbling more than 5%. Broadcom fell about 5.4%, TSMC about 7% and Intel about 8.1%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The rout is global and across the whole memory/storage chain — overnight Asia led down and the US session is following through, not stabilizing.

headlines.headline: AppLovin is still up about 28.9% at $349.66 after Q3 revenue jumped 55% to $2.18 billion (vs $2.07 billion expected), EPS of $4.30 beat the $4.03 consensus, and it guided Q4 revenue to $2.365-2.395 billion (vs $2.25 billion expected) plus a $3.2 billion buyback add.
headlines.why_it_matters: The morning's clearest earnings counterweight is still holding most of its gain — a genuine blowout with a raised guide — but it is one name against a broad tape.

headlines.headline: Initial jobless claims fell to 189,000 last week, the fewest since mid-July, the Labor Department reported at 8:30 AM ET — a strong labor print heading into Friday's payrolls.
headlines.why_it_matters: A genuinely strong labor print that would normally support the tape, but it is being ignored while chips dominate the session — a sign the move is sentiment- and positioning-driven, not macro-driven.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news this morning; the Nov 3 Q3 story carries forward: record revenue $357.2M (+43% year over year, vs ~$348.32M consensus), record Adjusted EBITDA $197.3M, DCF coverage 1.67x, EPS $0.33 vs $0.3345 expected, distribution held at $0.525, full-year guidance tightened to Adjusted EBITDA $770-780M and DCF $495-505M. The $0.525 distribution pays tomorrow, Friday Nov 6. On the earnings call, management said over 60% of 2027 horsepower deliveries are contracted (about 90% of first-half deliveries), but flagged cost pressure: monthly lubricant costs exited Q3 about 25% above first-half levels and diesel hit an all-time high in September, with pricing not yet fully reflecting the increases.
